que-es.claim: Why Adeorq: the raw power of CLIs paired with desktop app comfort.
que-es.lead: Major AI breakthroughs always launch on CLI tools before reaching official desktop apps. Adeorq brings day-one CLI access into a sleek desktop cockpit, enabling parallel agent squads, zero token waste, and full local control.
que-es.p1.sub: New AI models (like Opus 5) and 1M context upgrades land on CLI tools weeks before desktop GUI apps. Get immediate access without waiting for third-party updates.
que-es.p2.titulo: Parallel Agent Squads vs Single Chat
que-es.p2.sub: Instead of waiting on a single linear chat window, Adeorq lets you run 3, 5, or 9 agents simultaneously in dedicated panes with live turn-completion alerts.
que-es.p3.sub: Resume local session transcripts in one click. Maintain surgical control over prompt context so you maximize your subscription without burning quota.
que-es.p4.sub: Runs native Windows ConPTY terminals inheriting your PowerShell profile, PATH, scripts, and SSH keys. No account creation, no external API keys, around 4 MB Rust binary.
features.titulo: A high-performance cockpit engineered to orchestrate AI agents.
features.lead: Purpose-built for serious vibe coding. Every workflow tool is designed around speed, clarity, and agent autonomy.
features.conpty.texto: Each pane runs the genuine Windows console subsystem. Enjoy crisp rendering, full color support, instant redrawing, Ctrl+C handling, and true shell resizing that never chokes on thousands of log lines.
features.conpty.item1: PowerShell, CMD, or Git Bash with your full environment PATH & profiles
features.conpty.item2: True pseudoterminal reflow without line wrapping or truncation
features.conpty.item3: Copy, paste, drag & drop screenshots directly to your active agent
features.sesiones.texto: Adeorq automatically detects local CLI session transcripts on your machine. See titles, active project states, and resume any session in one click — with uncommitted change warnings to keep your workspace safe.
features.sesiones.item1: Live title, project path, and status indicators for every session
features.sesiones.item2: One-click resume with full context memory preserved
features.sesiones.item3: Uncommitted Git change detection before archiving any workspace
features.escuadron.titulo: Parallel squad grid with turn alerts
features.escuadron.texto: Run multiple agent sessions side-by-side in custom grid layouts. Glowing visual indicators alert you the moment an agent finishes its turn, so you never waste time tab-switching.
features.escuadron.item1: Flexible grid panes splittable horizontally or vertically
features.escuadron.item2: Instant turn-completion glowing alerts across all active panes
features.escuadron.item3: Color-coded project badges for instant visual identification
features.agenda.titulo: Ideas Tray: capture thoughts on the fly
features.agenda.texto: As agents work, spontaneous ideas and next steps arise. Instead of interrupting your flow, ideas land in a project-bound tray to review when ready. Agents propose, you approve.
features.agenda.item1: Project-bound tray for background ideas and next action items
features.agenda.item3: Agents propose ideas safely without touching private credentials
features.sistema.texto: Boots instantly with Windows. Built natively with Rust & Tauri — lightweight around 4 MB footprint with zero browser overhead. Signed updates install seamlessly with full release notes.
features.sistema.item1: Optional system startup with instant window restore
features.sistema.item3: Native around 4 MB app — ultra-low RAM footprint and zero bloat
features.lienzo.texto: Arrange terminals freely on an infinite canvas. Wire agents together with visual relay arrows, sketch freehand notes, and use built-in widgets like Pomodoro, Stopwatches, Calculators, and Calendars right where you work.
features.lienzo.item1: Infinite canvas layout with visual agent-to-agent relay connections
features.lienzo.item2: Excalidraw-style freehand drawing, lines, frames, and typography notes
features.lienzo.item3: Built-in productivity widgets: Pomodoro, Stopwatch, Calculator, and Daily Notes

descarga.gratis: Free & open development. No trial period, no credit card required.

changelog.lead: Dozens of versions shipped since it started. This is not a site with a product behind it: it is a product being used while it is built.

roadmap.lead: Milestones driven by user value. Each goal unlocks once its technical condition is fulfilled.
roadmap.0.texto: Automatically saving node coordinates, terminal states, and drawing layers upon closing the app so you resume exactly where you left off.
roadmap.1.texto: A group of sessions devoted to one big job, apart from everything else: you go in and you only see theirs. Half the piece already exists, because the Foreman groups what it hands out; what is missing is for the group to survive a restart and to be creatable by hand.
roadmap.2.texto: Eliminating Windows SmartScreen first-install warnings with a verified Code Signing certificate.
roadmap.3.texto: Porting the PTY engine beyond Windows ConPTY to PTY/TTY for macOS and Linux based on community demand.
faq.lead: Everything you need to know about Adeorq.
faq.0.p: Do I need an API key or extra subscription?
faq.0.r: No. Adeorq interfaces with the CLI tools already installed on your system. It never asks for API keys, stores no credentials, and routes no code through external servers. You use your existing CLI authorization.
faq.1.p: Can I run other CLIs besides Claude Code?
faq.1.r: Yes. Terminals are native ConPTY shells, so you can execute Antigravity, Codex, Gemini, Python, Node, or custom scripts. Claude Code has deeper session reading today because it uses open transcript files.
faq.2.p: Why does Windows SmartScreen display a warning on install?
faq.2.r: SmartScreen flags newly published executables without an established download volume prior to EV certificate signing. Updates are cryptographically signed. You can verify SHA-256 hashes against our official GitHub releases.
faq.3.p: Is there a macOS or Linux build?
faq.3.r: Not currently. Adeorq is optimized specifically for Windows ConPTY. A cross-platform port to Unix PTY is planned as demand grows.
faq.4.p: What are the system resource requirements?
faq.4.r: The installer is around 4 MB. Powered by Tauri & Rust, memory consumption is minimal (~40 MB base). Performance depends entirely on the CLI processes you run.
faq.5.p: Does any codebase data leave my machine?
faq.5.r: Never. Adeorq operates strictly on your local file system. It includes Streamer Mode to instantly redact sensitive file paths, environment keys, and project names during live streams or screen shares.

roadmap.4.texto: Claude Code keeps its conversations in files, which is why they can be read. Codex now shows up too, inside its project and with its client mark. Antigravity and Gemini each keep theirs their own way: they will be added as they can be read without making anything up.
features.cuentas.titulo: Several accounts, and the keys where they belong
features.cuentas.texto: One card per installed program, with how much of its limits you have used. You can have several accounts of the same one and split the work between them.
features.cuentas.item1: API keys go encrypted into the Windows Credential Manager
features.cuentas.item2: Never in a configuration file, and they do not come back out
features.cuentas.item3: Whatever you have not installed yet, with its download button
